correctness.rationale: For the eight corners of an axis-parallel box, all squared distances are the seven nonempty subset sums of A=a²,B=b²,C=c². The only variable comparison after 0<A≤B≤C is C versus A+B. At each threshold the VR complex is the flag complex of the F₂³ Cayley graph generated by coordinate differences of weight ≤t. The early components are four edges, two squares, then either the cube graph wedge of five S¹ or two tetrahedra; after both C and A+B there are two filled tetrahedra linked by four bridges, wedge of three S¹. At A+C the forbidden edges form two C4 and their independence complex join S⁰*S⁰≈S¹. At B+C four disjoint forbidden antipodal edges yield (S⁰)^{*4}=S³ until full simplex at A+B+C. Integral face boundary module of cube has six oriented square boundaries and one primitive relation; adding 12,13,23 face diagonals kills respectively 2,2,1 primitive H1 generators and creates no new ones. Coordinate edges merge H0 at a,b,c. This reconstructs all H0/H1/H3 bars, zero H2, free integral stage homology and field-independence, including simultaneous distance thresholds.

value.rationale: Complete intrinsic Euclidean topological persistence for every 3D orthotope vertex set is a motivated all-aspect-ratio classification, revealing a sharp Pythagorean wall where a five-circle intermediate stage is replaced by two contractible components. Exact interval endpoints, multiplicities and integral torsion control are useful geometric-topological benchmark facts beyond the already known regular cube.

limitations: Only eight Euclidean corners of rectangular axis-parallel 3D box; no higher dimensional, filled box, general parallelepiped or graph-metric extension.
The barcode over fields follows from integral primitive cycle analysis; F₂ tests alone would miss torsion.
